correctness.rationale: Every biderivation is specified by \(h=\{x,y\}\), and descent requires \(2xh=2yh=0\). The Jacobiator is an alternating triderivation on a two-generated algebra and therefore vanishes. In characteristic two all parameters occur; the automorphism group has order \(q^2|\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb F_q)|\), and direct Jacobian transport proves invariance of \(z\). The three fixed-parameter orbit sizes are \(1\), \(q^2-1\), and \((q-1)q^2\), with proven transitivity. In odd characteristic the annihilator intersection forces \(h=zxy\), and monomial linear automorphisms act by \(z\mapsto\pm z\). An actual packaged standalone checker independently enumerated all brackets and automorphisms over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_4\), including alternation and the Jacobi identity, and checked all odd-field sign orbits over \(\mathbb F_3\), \(\mathbb F_5\), and \(\mathbb F_7\); final output was VERIFY_ALL_OK. The symbolic proof covers arbitrary finite fields; finite enumerations are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The fixed algebra \(A=k[x,y]/(x^2,y^2)\) is a canonical four-dimensional short complete intersection and, in characteristic two, the modular group algebra of \(C_2\times C_2\). The exhaustive Poisson-isomorphism classes are natural moduli data. The socle coefficient \(z\) stays fixed under all nonlinear algebra automorphisms even for unit-valued brackets, an unexpected absolute invariant. The sharp change from \(q^4\) labeled brackets and \(3q\) classes in characteristic two to \(q\) labeled brackets and \((q+1)/2\) classes in odd characteristic provides a structural boundary. No general downstream theorem is required or asserted.
